    Representation-finiteness and two-sided ideals #

    Every finite-dimensional module over a representation-finite algebra is a finite direct sum of members of a fixed finite indecomposable family. Since annihilators turn direct sums into intersections and every two-sided ideal is the annihilator of its regular quotient, the two-sided ideal lattice is finite.

    IsRepresentationFinite k (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)

    Representation-finiteness descends to every algebra quotient.
